clue.text: Warden and police finally intercepting joyrider?

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word just before it
to intercept is to get in the way, so one piece cuts into the middle of the other

blocks.note: a joyrider takes a car, so whimsically a car-taker, hence the question mark
the last letter of police

explanation.surface: A warden and the police at last catch a youth who has stolen a car for a spin.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical coinage: a joyrider literally takes cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A caretaker looks after a building or property, much as a warden has charge of a place.

clue.text: Colour up after incapacitating heart with drink

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only the middle letters are kept
in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards
after places one piece behind another in the final order

blocks.note: the two middle letters of incapacitating
red is a colour

explanation.surface: Someone flushes red after a drink knocks them out.
explanation.definitionFit: Cider is an alcoholic drink made from fermented apple juice.

clue.text: Want regular free paper

indicators.note: regular means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters of free
a quire is a quantity of paper, 24 or 25 sheets

explanation.surface: Someone wants a regular free newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper' suggests a newspaper, but it is a quire, the paper-trade measure.
explanation.definitionFit: To require something is to need it, and want can mean need or lack.

clue.text: Creep like an amphibian?

blocks.note: first meaning: a sycophant who fawns on superiors
second meaning, whimsical: resembling a certain warty amphibian

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a made-up adjective, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A toady is a flatterer who sucks up to people, which is what a creep is in British slang.

clue.text: Don't say anything to delay old lady

blocks.note: to keep someone is to delay or detain them
old lady is slang for mother

explanation.surface: A warning not to mention anything that might hold up an elderly woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Keep mum is a British idiom for staying silent, so it is an instruction to say nothing.

clue.text: Going there and back to get drinks from the bar?

definitions.text: to get drinks from the bar

blocks.note: first meaning: a journey out and home again

blocks.clueFragment: to get drinks from the bar?
blocks.note: second meaning, cryptic: a trip made to fetch a round

explanation.walkthrough: A round is a set of drinks bought for a group, so a trip for it is a cryptic second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A round trip is a journey to a place and back again to the start.

clue.text: Understood one's out for diplomacy

indicators.note: out says a piece is removed and no longer present in the word

blocks.note: tacit means understood without being stated
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Something understood without words passes for diplomacy.
explanation.walkthrough: TACIT loses its I to leave TACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tact is skill in handling people sensitively, the core quality of a good diplomat.

clue.text: Label on French water is an artistic scene

blocks.note: a tab is a label
l'eau is French for the water

explanation.surface: A label on a bottle of French water makes an artistic picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a picturesque grouping of people or objects, as in a painting or stage scene.

clue.text: Debated criminal's fine and made a mistake

blocks.note: a con is a convict
F is fine, as in pencil grades
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A court debated whether the criminal's fine was a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: To confer is to consult or talk things over together, so conferred means discussed or debated.

clue.text: One day with English queen swilling tea's enough

indicators.note: swilling sloshes liquid round, so the letters are swirled into a new order

blocks.note: one is a
D is the abbreviation for day
E is the abbreviation for English
Qu is an abbreviation for queen
taken as written

explanation.surface: Spending one day with an English queen gulping tea is quite sufficient.
explanation.definitionFit: Adequate means sufficient for the purpose, which is what enough describes.

clue.text: Sophisticated characters found in suburban enclave

indicators.note: the letters needed are already sitting inside the following words, just waiting to be found

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Smart, cultivated types are to be found in a well-heeled suburban enclave.
explanation.definitionFit: Urbane describes someone polished, courteous and worldly, which is exactly being sophisticated.

clue.text: Brilliant in binary code

indicators.note: putting something in code scrambles it, so the letters are encrypted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shows off their brilliance by writing in binary code.
explanation.definitionFit: Brainy is an informal word for highly intelligent, so it matches brilliant in the clever sense.

clue.text: Angered by report of absurd death

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the words are judged by how they come across when spoken

blocks.note: absurd is mad, and a death is an end

explanation.surface: Someone is furious on hearing of a ridiculous death.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, a mad end runs together into the past form of 'madden'; the extra -ED is glossed over by the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To madden is to make someone furious, so a person maddened has been made angry.

clue.text: One's hiding key by south entrance

indicators.note: something hiding another keeps it tucked inside itself
by means next to, so one piece is set alongside the other

blocks.note: an ace is a one in cards, and one's makes it plural-sounding: aces
C is a musical key
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Someone hides a key by the southern entrance for a visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'One's' is not a link: it is read as a possessive S turning ACE into ACES.
explanation.definitionFit: Access is a means or way of getting in, so a door or entrance gives access.

clue.text: Couple wantonly gobbling ultimate burger won't half get fat

indicators.note: wantonly means recklessly, without restraint, so the letters are thrown into disorder
ultimate means last, so the closing letter of the next word is used
gobbling swallows something, so one piece ends up inside the other
half means only part of the word survives and the rest is cut

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of burger
taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A greedy couple devouring burgers will hardly avoid putting on weight.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the second half of won't, NT, is kept. 'Won't half' is also British slang for 'certainly will'.
explanation.definitionFit: Corpulent means stout or overweight, an adjective for being fat.

clue.text: Facial hair deficiency is burden on son

indicators.note: a deficiency is a defect, so the letters come out faulty and rearranged
on means placed next to, so one piece follows the other

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A father frets that his son's lack of facial hair weighs on him.
explanation.definitionFit: Sideburns are strips of hair grown down the sides of a man's face in front of the ears.

clue.text: Waiting room for people who are late?

definitions.text: Waiting room for people who are late?

blocks.clueFragment: Waiting room for people who are late?
blocks.note: surface reading: a lounge for those who turn up behind schedule
setter's reading: 'the late' are the dead, kept in a room until burial

explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' means deceased, as in 'the late Mr Smith'.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where bodies are kept until burial or cremation is a room where the dead wait.

clue.text: Make an assumption before umpire arrives

blocks.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
an umpire judges a contest

explanation.surface: Someone jumps to conclusions before the referee even turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: To prejudge is to form a verdict in advance, without the evidence, which is assuming.

clue.text: Short career on cash register's over, followed by year of fun!

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the last letter is dropped
over means turned over, so the word is read backwards
followed by puts the next piece directly after the previous ones

blocks.note: a job is a career
a till is a cash register; the 's is 'is'
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A brief career at the checkout is over, and then comes a year of fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Jollity is cheerful merriment, which is what fun means as a noun.

clue.text: Watches returning hero beheaded — it's an ugly sight

indicators.note: beheading takes off the head, so the first letter is lost
returning goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: to eye is to watch
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spectator watches a returning hero who has been decapitated, a grisly sight.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is something unpleasant to look at, especially an ugly building.

clue.text: Take off staff with salary protection

indicators.note: protection wraps around and shields something, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: salary is pay
a staff is a rod or stick

explanation.surface: An employer cuts staff while offering protection for salaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' looks like removal; here it means mimic.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to impersonate them for comic effect, which a parody does.

clue.text: Break soldier with meanness

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, British Army soldiers
spite is meanness or malice

explanation.surface: A soldier breaks ranks out of malice.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a short rest or interval of relief, a break from something hard.

clue.text: Easily fooled listener about libel order

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards
to order something is to rearrange it, so the letters are put in a new sequence

blocks.note: lug is British slang for an ear, the listener
taken as written

explanation.surface: A credulous listener is taken in by a libel order.
explanation.definitionFit: Gullible describes someone readily deceived or taken in, which is being easily fooled.

clue.text: Stop believer in God overshadowing saint

indicators.note: to overshadow is to loom over and cover, so one piece is wrapped round the other

blocks.note: a deist believes in a God known through reason
S is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A believer tells someone to stop casting a saint into the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: DEIST goes round S, splitting as DE-S-IST.
explanation.definitionFit: To desist is to cease doing something, a formal verb meaning stop.

clue.text: Very fond of little Dorothy's notes

blocks.note: Dot is a pet form of Dorothy
E and D are musical notes

explanation.surface: Someone treasures the notes written by little Dorothy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition needs 'on' to follow: doted on means was very fond of.
explanation.definitionFit: To dote is to lavish love on someone, so doted means was extremely fond of.

clue.text: Bargain for least outlay

indicators.note: to lay out is to set things out afresh, so the letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shopper wants a bargain for the smallest spend.
explanation.definitionFit: A steal is informal for something bought very cheaply, a real bargain.

clue.text: Older person in state housing gets tax at zero rate, initially

indicators.note: a housing is an outer casing, so only the shell of the word is used
initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: the outside letters of state
NI is National Insurance, a UK tax on earnings
zero looks like the letter O
the first letter of rate

explanation.surface: A pensioner in council housing pays no tax.
explanation.walkthrough: National Insurance (NI) is a UK payroll tax. 'State housing' sounds like council flats, but housing asks for the shell of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior is used as a noun for an elderly person, as in senior citizen.

clue.text: Ravel viol duet went on longer

indicators.note: to ravel is to tangle, so the letters are knotted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A duet for viols by the composer Ravel runs on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: Ravel looks like the French composer but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlive is to survive beyond someone or something, so outlived means lasted or went on longer.

clue.text: For example, put time in to give support

indicators.note: putting something in means placing it inside the other piece

blocks.note: say is used to introduce an example
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An instruction to invest time in order to back someone up.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay something is to prop or brace it; a stay is a supporting rope or brace.

clue.text: Drug's given healthy bloom

blocks.note: speed is slang for amphetamine
well means healthy

explanation.surface: A drug is credited with producing a healthy flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedwell is a small blue-flowered plant, so it is an example of a bloom.
